data.claim: The two surfaces disagree only when the first (CLI) probe is inconclusive: an inconclusive result is never cached, so the MCP call re-probes live and can get a conclusive answer; a conclusive CLI result is cached (TTL 300s) and the MCP call reads it, so they agree.
data.falsifier: A companion whose probe is conclusive on the CLI call and different on the MCP call making the unseeded test fail; or a CLI-inconclusive/MCP-conclusive companion NOT making it fail
data.mechanism: companions.scan caches only inst is not None; is_installed returns None on timeout or spawn failure
data.probe: 1) flip companion with sh -c probe that succeeds once then fails: unseeded test PASSED (cache hit, as claimed). 2) flip companion whose probe cannot be spawned (exec format error) during the CLI call and exits 0 during the MCP call: unseeded test FAILED with flipflop state unknown vs installed, matching the pre-push failure (context7 unknown vs installed). With the cache seeded for every companion: 43/43 parity tests pass.
data.question: Why does the ddflow_companions CLI/MCP parity test fail intermittently?

evidence.note: R324f3d0fe9 CONFIRMED: unseeded test with a companion that is unspawnable on the CLI call and answers on the MCP call fails (flipflop unknown vs installed), matching pre-push context7 unknown vs installed; a conclusive-then-different probe does not fail (cache hit).

recall: decisions D-no-own-services-local-dir/D-roborev-local not touched (test seeds .ddflow/local/companion-probes.json inside a tmp repo only); lesson L185edcda1d followed (suite run with PYTHONPATH unset).

463d910: test seeds the probe cache for every companion via companions._write_cache before either surface runs; adds a project companion 'flipflop' (exec-format-error probe during CLI call, valid script during MCP call) so the regression is deterministic, not load-dependent.

ruff check + ruff format --check on tests/test_api_layer.py: clean; pre-commit run --files: exit 0; roborev job 878 on 463d910: no issues found (it also mutation-tested the guard: probe_cache_ttl_s=0 makes ddflow_companions fail unknown vs installed).
2843 passed, 1 skipped in 81.7s on 463d910 (PYTHONPATH unset); unseeded variant of the parity test fails (flipflop unknown vs installed), fixed passes 43/43.

Checked: seeding happens after init and before both surfaces (cache under the tmp repo's .ddflow/local, TTL 300s default >> test runtime); every other tool in the parametrisation unaffected (43/43 pass); flipflop's absolute detect path is the tmp repo, so no cross-test interference under xdist; roborev job 878 found none.

No other test compares two live companion probes; tests/test_companions.py probes with stubs. One test file changed, no helper duplicated (uses companions._write_cache, the writer itself, so the cache format cannot drift).

data.summary: ddflow merge run from inside the item's worktree merges successfully ('merged B-fix-flaky-companions-parity (463d910e) into main'), then removes that worktree and exits 1 with 'pwd: error retrieving current directory: getcwd: cannot access parent directories' -- a successful merge reported as a failure, so a script or agent checking the exit code retries or stops on a merge that landed.
